chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three [types of women] are married in all states: the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the like of her who does not menstruate; and the one who has not yet menstruated, and the like of her who does not menstruate; and the one who has not been entered into by her husband.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of women who can be married according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the marital eligibility of women by categorizing them based on menstrual status: post-menopausal women (typically after age 60), pre-pubertal girls (under age 9), and virgins who have not yet been consummated. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the absence of menstruation does not invalidate marriage, provided the woman is of an age or state where menstruation is not expected or has ceased, thereby facilitating valid unions even in cases of delayed puberty or menopause.
